# TexasBitcoin

> The authority on Bitcoin in Texas: the energy and mining base layer, the money law, and the programmable-money frontier being built on top. An independent research and reference publication — every datable claim is sourced to primary documents or reputable journalism. Not financial, investment, legal, or tax advice.

## Core reference

- [The History of Bitcoin in Texas](https://texasbitcoin.com/history-of-bitcoin-in-texas): The definitive, sourced account — from Supervisory Memorandum 1037 (2014) through the mining migration to Rockdale (2021), ERCOT demand response, and the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (SB 21, 2025). 21 cited sources.
- [What Texas Law Actually Says About Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/what-texas-law-says-about-bitcoin): The legal status of Bitcoin in Texas from the primary record — legal to buy, sell, hold, and mine; no state license to sell your own coin (Supervisory Memorandum 1037); custody, UCC, proof of reserves, legal tender vs. reserve asset, taxes, and the federal 18 U.S.C. § 1960 seam. 13 cited sources.
- [The Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-strategic-bitcoin-reserve): How the state's Bitcoin reserve works and where it stands — SB 21 (signed June 20, 2025), the $10M appropriation, the $500B market-cap floor, the first ~$5M purchase via the iShares Bitcoin Trust (November 20, 2025), the five-member advisory committee, and the move from a Bitcoin ETF to direct custody. A tracked reference. 9 cited sources.
- [Who Holds the Texas Bitcoin Reserve?](https://texasbitcoin.com/who-holds-the-texas-bitcoin-reserve): The living custody watch on the reserve — no custodian named as of August 30, 2026; RFP 908-26-1778WS (posted May 7, 2026, closed July 10, 2026; issued by the Comptroller on behalf of the Texas Treasury Safekeeping Trust Company), contract execution targeted for late August 2026, the 60-day IBIT-to-direct-Bitcoin conversion clock, the required public holdings website, cold-storage/security scope, and what Texas owns (an ETF claim) vs. what it will control (coin in the state's name). Updated as the award lands. 9 cited sources.
- [Elon Musk, Tesla, and the Bitcoin Energy Question](https://texasbitcoin.com/elon-musk-bitcoin-energy): The sourced account of Tesla's Bitcoin treasury (the $1.5B purchase, Feb 2021; accepting then suspending BTC payments over energy, May 2021; the ~75% sale for $936M, Q2 2022; 11,509 BTC still held in 2026 — all from SEC filings), Musk's 2021 energy reversal and the Cambridge index (cbeci.org) he shared, the greening of Bitcoin's energy mix (Cambridge: 52.4% sustainable in 2025) with its honest counterweight, and how Musk's own AI data centers (xAI's Colossus) now dwarf Bitcoin's energy use — colliding with Bitcoin mining on the Texas ERCOT grid. 28 cited sources.
- [Ross Ulbricht, Silk Road, and Bitcoin's First Use Case](https://texasbitcoin.com/ross-ulbricht-silk-road-bitcoin): The sourced account of the Austin-born (UT Dallas physics, 2006) founder of Silk Road — Bitcoin's first application at scale (Tor + Bitcoin, 2011–2013, mostly illegal drugs) — kept honest about what Silk Road was. Arrest (Oct 1, 2013), conviction on all seven counts (Feb 4, 2015), the two-life-plus-40-years sentence under Judge Katherine Forrest, the precise murder-for-hire record (alleged, never charged/tried/convicted, no one killed), the seized Bitcoin (~174,000 BTC auctioned 2014–15; the separate 69,370 BTC seized 2020, now in the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve), the Free Ross campaign led by his mother Lyn Ulbricht (~607,000-signature petition), and the full and unconditional pardon (Jan 21, 2025) and Bitcoin 2025 speech. Includes the primary video of his post-pardon keynote. 28 cited sources.
- [Ted Cruz and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/ted-cruz-bitcoin): Did Ted Cruz fall out of Bitcoin, or sell out? The sourced record answers: from self-described skeptic ("I didn't understand it very much," Oct 2021) to the Senate's loudest champion — the Aug 9, 2021 infrastructure-bill floor fight ("not greater than five" senators could define a cryptocurrency), disclosed purchases (up to $50,000 on Jan 25, 2022, via River; $50,001–$100,000 in 2023), the CBDC Anti-Surveillance State Act (S. 3801, Feb 2024), the Commerce Committee chairmanship (Jan 2025), the FLARE Act (S. 1188, Mar 2025), and the four-year CBDC ban that became law July 11, 2026 (Public Law 119-101) — which Cruz voted against because it wasn't permanent. The honest counterweight: the $350,000 Jeff Yass-funded Bitcoin Freedom PAC contribution and the Armstrong/Winklevoss max donations that followed his positions in the most expensive Senate race ever ($192M raised). 26 cited sources.

- [Greg Abbott and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/greg-abbott-bitcoin): The Governor Who Took It First — the sourced twelve-year arc: the 2014 campaign accepting bitcoin donations (Apr 17, 2014, ~$2,000 collected, "The spirit of Bitcoin embodies the free market principles..."), the “Count me in as a crypto law proposal supporter” endorsement (Mar 2021), the legal foundation signed June 2021 (HB 4474 virtual-currency UCC + HB 1576 blockchain working group), the post-Uri recruitment of Bitcoin miners as controllable grid load (fall 2021), the SB 21 + HB 4488 signatures creating and shielding the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (June 20, 2025), and the honest counterweight: the June 10, 2026 directive making data centers fund their own grid costs rather than residential ratepayers. 15 cited sources.

- [Dan Patrick and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/dan-patrick-bitcoin): The Asset, Not the Megawatts — the two-sided record resolved by its dates: the SB 1751 brake (Senate passage 30–1, Apr 12, 2023, the 10% demand-response cap that died in a House committee), the “Wild Wild West of data centers and crypto miners crashing our grid” warning (June 2024, ~2,600 MW mining load on ERCOT), then the pivot to the asset: Texas Bitcoin Reserve named a legislative priority (Jan 30, 2025), SB 21's bipartisan Senate passage (Mar 6, 2025) with the “digital gold” statement, and delivery (signed June 20, 2025). Thesis: bullish on the coin, tough on the load — one coherent position, not a flip. Honest counterweight: the industry's demand-response-is-a-service case against him. 12 cited sources.

- [Kelly Hancock and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/kelly-hancock-bitcoin): The Man Who Bought Texas Its Bitcoin — the execution record of the acting Texas Comptroller: succession from Glenn Hegar (chief clerk June 19, 2025; acting comptroller July 1, 2025, eleven days after SB 21), the first state Bitcoin purchase in U.S. history (~$5M in IBIT at $51.8694/share, Nov 20, 2025), the build to the full $10M appropriation, the advisory committee he chairs (four outside members named May 28, 2026) and custody RFP 908-26-1778WS (contract execution targeted late Aug 2026). Honest counterweight: the lame-duck steward — Hancock lost the Mar 3, 2026 GOP primary to Don Huffines (~58%–23%, Trump endorsement over Abbott's $2.6M in ads), resigned effective July 31, 2026, and handed the reserve to Huffines on Aug 1 with the custodian still unnamed. 18 cited sources.

- [Don Huffines and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/don-huffines-bitcoin): The Citadel Candidate Gets the Keys — the sourced Bitcoin record of the Texas Comptroller sworn in Aug 1, 2026 (Abbott appointment, July 2, to the term Kelly Hancock resigned effective July 31) who now has statutory custody of the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (SB 21 § 403.703) and sits on its advisory committee by office (§ 403.707). The 2022 governor-campaign Bitcoin plan ("the citadel for Bitcoin," Dec 16, 2021 tweet; six planks published Jan 28, 2022 incl. legal tender, a Bitcoin & Cryptocurrency Policy Commission, and holding a portion of state reserves in Bitcoin — three years before SB 21); Senate District 16 (2015–19); third in the 2022 governor primary (12%); Trump endorsement (Feb 27, 2026) and the ~58%–23% primary win (Mar 3, 2026). Watch items: custody RFP 908-26-1778WS's late-August execution target passed with no award as of Sept 1, 2026; the Nov 3, 2026 general vs. Sarah Eckhardt; the first SB 21 biennial report due Dec 31, 2026. Honest counterweight: the silence — zero public words on the reserve since taking office. 19 cited sources.

- [Jimmy Song and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/jimmy-song-bitcoin): The Man Who Teaches Bitcoin From Scratch — the first builders-wing people page: the sourced record of the Austin-based developer, educator, and author of Programming Bitcoin (O'Reilly, Mar 26, 2019; repo since Dec 2017, ~1,900 stars), who taught "Programming Blockchain" as a 7-week graduate course at UT Austin's McCombs School (early 2019), trained 500+ developers in his two-day seminar, and authored 14 Bitcoin Core test-suite commits (Apr–Jun 2017). The block-size-war essays and the Aug 24, 2017 "Why I Was Wrong" self-grade; the Lubin wager (810.8 ETH vs 69.74 BTC, deadline May 23, 2023, outcome disputed); five books through Fiat Ruins Everything (Sept 2023); the Oct 8, 2021 Texas Blockchain Summit exchange with Ted Cruz; "altcoin scammer central" as Consensus moved to Austin (June 2022). Honest counterweight: the maximalist's ledger — the disputed bet, the Blockchain Capital seat, and a "Core developer" billing that outruns fourteen test commits. 20 cited sources.

- [The Satoshi Nakamoto Institute](https://texasbitcoin.com/satoshi-nakamoto-institute): The Canon Was Written in Austin — the sourced history of the Austin 501(c)(3) founded Nov 2013 by Michael Goldstein, Daniel Krawisz, and Pierre Rochard out of the Mises Circle, a UT Austin Austrian-economics reading group. The Complete Satoshi (whitepaper, emails, forum posts, code, 2008–2012), the Library (Chaum 1982 → Szabo, Dai, Back, Finney, beside Mises/Hayek/Rothbard: "Bitcoin was not forged in a vacuum"), and the Mempool canon: Krawisz's "Hyperbitcoinization" (Mar 29, 2014, coined the term), Rochard's "Speculative Attack" (July 4, 2014), Goldstein's "Everyone's a Scammer" (Sept 11, 2014); later Parker Lewis (2020) and Gigi (2021). Schism: Krawisz's last essay Jan 8, 2017; "I like forks" (Aug 2017); BSV advocate by 2020 ("BTC betrayed me"; "lost the allies with whom I started the Institute") — all 34 of his Mempool entries still hosted (76 essays total, counted Sept 2026; Parker Lewis's full 16-part Gradually, Then Suddenly ran there 2019–2020). Relaunch: 501(c)(3) Mar 4, 2024; 21M-sat redesign; translations in 15+ languages; OpenSats Education Initiative grant July 5, 2024 (213M sats total); new site July 26, 2024; The Reorg podcast Feb 12, 2025; FY2024 revenue ~$138K. Texas thread: Rochard → Riot Platforms VP Research (Rockdale's owner) → The Bitcoin Bond Company; Lewis/Unchained; Song at UT. 20 cited sources.

- [Charles Schwertner and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/charles-schwertner-bitcoin): The Surgeon Who Wrote the Reserve — the sourced record of the Georgetown orthopedic surgeon, Senate District 5 (since Jan 2013), and Business and Commerce chair who authored Senate Bill 21: SB 778 (filed Jan 2025, donations + 1%-of-revenue cap + cold storage) refiled as SB 21 (Feb 12, 2025; coauthors Hinojosa, Parker, West; House sponsor Capriglione); committee Feb 18 ("We can buy land, we can buy gold"; Hegar testifies; $21M seed; 10–0); Senate 25–5 (Mar 6: "one-percent savings account"); House 101–42 (May 21); conference strips donations, trims $21M→$10M; signed June 20, 2025 alongside SB 6 (89R), the large-load law he joint-authored with King. Grid record: SB 3 (2021), the April 2023 grid package (10 GW Texas Energy Insurance Program), SB 1751 through his committee (30–1). Oct 10, 2025: "We took the full punch"; ether admissible only if it holds $500B for 24 months. Honest counterweight: Texans for Fiscal Responsibility's OPPOSE, Allen/Johnson on whales and donations, the reserve at ~$7.8M on $10M by Mar 2, 2026, and the leash on the load. On the Nov 3, 2026 SD-5 ballot. 22 cited sources.

- [Before the State: Texas's Grassroots Bitcoin Economy, 2013–2015](https://texasbitcoin.com/early-bitcoin-merchants-texas): The merchant layer of the record, told before the state had a position — Brave New Books (1904 Guadalupe) as the only known Texas Bitcoin vendor with two customers (KUT, June 6, 2013; consultant Michael Goldstein, later SNI co-founder); the Austin meetup at 189 members in Scholz Garten's back room (Dec 26, 2013); Techzette's eleven mapped Austin merchants (Feb 11, 2014: gun store, Rainey Street tacos + donuts, Havi Hair, Unconventional Oven, La Canasta); the Leander/Cedar Park BitPay cluster (Community Impact, Feb 17, 2014: Vista Ridge Dentistry, La Canasta Meat Market, Hill Country Home Improvements; 1% vs ~2.5%); the first US Bitcoin ATM at HandleBar (Feb 20, 2014) and the gun store's second (Mar 2); the first Texas Bitcoin Conference (Mar 5–6, 2014, COTA) — all before Supervisory Memo 1037 (Apr 3, 2014); Art of Tacos at ~1 Bitcoin sale/week, over half during SXSW (Techzette, July 22, 2014); Houston's 15–17 merchants and the Houston Bitcoin Embassy (Mar 29, 2015); Muenster's Crossroads Express Stop (single source). The SXSW 2015 Bitcoin pedicab ("Carrie," filmed by Austin advocate Scott Rose, posted Mar 14, 2015) handled as labeled lore: only source is the video; the forum's "over a bitcoin in tips" is unverifiable — the one posted address belongs to the poster and sent 0.01 BTC to the Dorian Nakamoto fund in March 2014. Honest counterweight: the volumes were tiny. 20 cited sources.

- [Central Texas Gun Works and Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/central-texas-gun-works-bitcoin): The First Gun Store in America to Take Bitcoin — the first grassroots-era merchant page: the sourced record of the South Austin firearms retailer and training school (owner Michael Cargill, 12-year Army veteran, store founded 2011) that began accepting Bitcoin online Jan 27, 2014 and in-store Jan 28 via BitPay — the first licensed firearms dealer in Texas, and per Forbes (Mar 9, 2014) "the first legal Bitcoin-friendly firearm retail business in the country." The first legal Bitcoin firearm sale in the US (Feb 4, 2014; remote buyer, personal wallet, full Form 4473/NICS check); the Robocoin ATM unveiled Texas Independence Day (Mar 2, 2014, 321 W. Ben White Blvd, ten days after HandleBar's first-in-the-US machine — both of America's Bitcoin ATMs briefly in Austin); BitPay freezing the account under its no-firearms terms (Mar 12, 2014) and the move to Coinvoice; NBC's pairing with TrackingPoint (Mar 30, 2014). Honest counterweight: Brady Campaign's Brian Malte — the payment method is irrelevant, Texas's private-sale gap is the issue; BitPay was within its terms. Coda: Cargill as respondent in Garland v. Cargill, 602 U.S. 406 (June 14, 2024, 6–3, bump stocks). Store still accepts Bitcoin. 14 cited sources.

- [The Dead File: Texas Bitcoin Bills That Didn't Become Law](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-bills-that-died): The 89th Legislature's Bitcoin dead file, every status verified on capitol.texas.gov: HJR 175 (constitutional right to own/hold/use a chosen medium of exchange incl. digital currency - passed the House May 9, 2025, left pending in Senate Business & Commerce May 15); the kiosk stalemate (SB 1705 passed the Senate, died on the House calendar May 27; HB 2798 passed the House Apr 25, died in Senate committee - two majorities, zero laws, ~$57M/yr kiosk-scam losses since); the reserve designs not chosen (HB 1598 Capriglione in-treasury/5-yr hold/donations, no hearing; HB 4258 Reynolds/Plesa ~$250M + $10M local authority, no hearing; SB 778 superseded by SB 21); and what was cut from SB 21 itself (staking removed; $21M rider trimmed to $10M). Framed as the 90th Legislature's (Jan 2027) draft agenda - nothing was voted down. 13 cited sources.

- [The Enforcement Ledger: Crypto Prosecutions in Texas](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-crypto-enforcement-report): The narrative/analysis layer on the case tracker - every number computed at build time from the tracker's dataset (152 DOJ-announced cases, 2013-present, ~$255M announced forfeitures) and re-derived on each data refresh: the acceleration curve (6 announced cases in 2013 -> 26 in 2025, the peak completed year) drawn as an original SVG chart, the charge mix (money laundering + unlicensed money transmission/18 U.S.C. § 1960 dominate; the registration-offense asterisk kept attached), the lumpy forfeitures (one ~$129M 2024 E.D. Tex. botnet case is ~half the all-time total - counts are the trend line, forfeitures are weather), the district map (Northern leads, Eastern overperforms), and an honest what-this-is-not section (press releases, not dockets). Cross-links: tracker, dead file, Doctor Bitcoin, reserve.

## Data assets

- [Texas Bitcoin Mining Map](https://texasbitcoin.com/bitcoin-mining-map-texas): Interactive, sourced map and dataset of every major industrial Bitcoin mine in Texas — operator, capacity, year online, and AI/HPC conversions — plus the August 2026 ERCOT data-center queue audit (474 GW queue, "Batch Zero" paused) and the miner-built AI campuses it screens (Hut 8 Beacon Point, Cipher Barber Lake, MARA Matagorda). Rockdale itself is now hybrid: AMD (50 MW, Jan 2026) + a 20-year, 191 MW, $9.1B frontier-AI-lab lease (Aug 10, 2026) while the mine keeps hashing; Corsicana's full 1 GW reported under LOI. CC BY 4.0, 26 cited sources.
- [Bitcoin Mining and ERCOT, in One Page](https://texasbitcoin.com/bitcoin-mining-ercot): The market companion to the mining map — how ERCOT treats miners as Large Flexible Loads (≥75 MW; task force first met April 14, 2022; interim interconnection process since March 25, 2022), the energy-only market fit, demand response and ancillary services (Riot's $31.7M August 2023 curtailment credits vs. 333 BTC mined), 4CP transmission-cost avoidance, scale (EIA: ~54B kWh forecast for 2025, ~10% of ERCOT consumption; 26,500 MW pipeline), SB 6 (signed June 20, 2025: financial commitments + ERCOT remote-disconnection switch for new large loads), and the honest counterweights: SB 1751's 30–1 Senate vote, and the AI-pivot eroding the fleet's flexibility. 13 cited sources.
- [Bitcoin Estate Planning in Texas: Buy, Hold, Die](https://texasbitcoin.com/bitcoin-estate-planning-texas): The sourced reference on Bitcoin across a Texas lifetime — no state license to sell your own coin (Supervisory Memorandum 1037), no state income tax (Prop 4, 2019) so gains face only federal tax (property per IRS Notice 2014-21), no state death tax (inheritance tax repealed Sept 1, 2015; Prop 8, Nov 4, 2025, constitutional ban), the permanent $15M/person federal estate exemption from Jan 1, 2026 (OBBBA), community property (Fam. Code § 3.003 presumption) with the § 1014(b)(6) double stepped-up basis, TRUFADAA (Estates Code ch. 2001, 2017) reaching custodians but not hardware wallets, and the self-custody inheritance problem stated honestly. Reference only — not legal or tax advice. 13 cited sources.
- [Gold as Tender, Bitcoin as Reserve](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-gold-vs-bitcoin): The essay on Texas's June 2025 hard-money split — SB 21 (Bitcoin reserve, signed June 20, 2025) and HB 1056 (gold/silver specie legal tender, signed June 22, 2025; tender effective Sept 1, 2026, depository-backed payment system targeted May 1, 2027) two days apart, with opposite verbs: spend vs. hold. Why Article I § 10's gold-and-silver tender clause gives metal a lane Bitcoin lacks (HJR 175's medium-of-exchange right died in the Senate), how both laws sit on a decade of custody-first plumbing (2015 Bullion Depository → 2026 reserve custodian; Capriglione on both threads), and the honest counterweight: both laws are still more statement than volume. 10 cited sources.
- [The Second Life of the Texas Mines](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-miners-ai-pivot): The longform on the miners-to-AI conversion — the mines were never the asset, the interconnection was. Rockdale's third act (AMD Jan 2026; the 20-year, 191 MW, $9.1B frontier-AI-lab lease announced Aug 10, 2026 — analysts name Anthropic; Riot's filings don't), the deal ledger (Core Scientific Denton $6.1B CoreWeave conversion + the Oct 30, 2025 shareholder rejection of CoreWeave's $9B acquisition; Galaxy Helios 526 MW / first 133 MW live July 2026; Cipher Black Pearl→Amazon and Barber Lake→Fluidstack ~$3B w/ Google backstop; Hut 8 Beacon Point $19.6B; MARA Matagorda up to 2 GW; Bitdeer Rockdale pipeline), the Stargate/Abilene Bitcoin-mining lineage (Lancium, Crusoe), and the honest counterweight: converted megawatts stop flexing — the grid's emergency brake (Riot's $31.7M August 2023) is a diminishing asset, met by SB 6 and the Aug 2026 ~474 GW queue audit. 15 cited sources.
- [Texas Bitcoin Bills 2027: The 90th Legislature Tracker](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-bills-2027): The living session-watch tracker — 0 bills yet (pre-filing opens November 9, 2026; session convenes January 12, 2027; filing deadline March 12; sine die May 31), every future bill to be verified on capitol.texas.gov. Ships with the sourced six-item watchlist grounded in the record: reserve top-up (the $10M seed vs. HB 4258's dead ~$250M design), the kiosk fight's third round (SB 1705/HB 2798 each passed one chamber in 2025), HJR 175's likely refiling, staking (cut from SB 21), post-SB 6 grid/large-load bills, and the reserve's first mandatory biennial report. Forward twin of the dead file. 8 cited sources.
- [Texas Bitcoin Law Timeline](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-law-timeline): Interactive timeline of every Bitcoin law, memo, and failed bill in Texas — Supervisory Memorandum 1037 (2014) through SB 21's Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and HB 1056 (2025), each verified against capitol.texas.gov or dob.texas.gov. 22 cited sources.
- [Texas Bitcoin Case Tracker](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-case-tracker): Living, filterable dataset of every federal 18 U.S.C. § 1960 (unlicensed money transmission) and crypto prosecution announced in Texas's four federal districts — built nightly from public DOJ press releases, every case linked to its primary source. CC BY-SA 4.0.

## Stories

- [The Rockdale Story](https://texasbitcoin.com/rockdale-texas-bitcoin): How a dying aluminum town became the Bitcoin mining capital of North America — Alcoa (1952–2008), Bitmain, Whinstone, and Riot's 700 MW flagship, sourced end to end. 13 cited sources.
- [Doctor Bitcoin](https://texasbitcoin.com/doctor-bitcoin): Voices of Texas Bitcoin, No. 1 — the sourced profile of Mark Alexander Hopkins and the gap between Texas money-transmission law and federal FinCEN registration. 7 cited sources.
- [The Doctor Bitcoin Tapes](https://texasbitcoin.com/doctor-bitcoin-interviews): The lore companion to the profile — every interview Hopkins has given about his case (Digital Cash Network, Free Talk Live, the Aria DiMezzo prison conversation, Gary Leland's pre-case episodes) blended into one story, with the CZ proportionality ledger and sourced Crypto Six context. A living page awaiting Hopkins's own from-the-hip additions. 22 cited sources.

## Directories

- [Texas Bitcoin Events](https://texasbitcoin.com/events): Free, open directory of Bitcoin meetups and conferences across Austin, Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, and San Antonio, linked directly to organizers.
- [The Exposure Map](https://texasbitcoin.com/invest-in-texas-bitcoin): Reference map of every route into the Texas Bitcoin economy — public mining equities with Texas operations (Riot, Core Scientific, Cipher, Galaxy, Bitdeer, MARA, Hut 8), Bitcoin itself and the state's own ETF-then-custody sequence, the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (closed to private money under SB 21's enrolled text), the Texas Bitcoin bond that doesn't exist, accredited-only venture funds, and the Texas Stock Exchange. Research and reference only — no recommendations, no exchange or broker links, not financial advice. 18 cited sources.
- [Texas Bitcoin Resources](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-bitcoin-resources): Curated reference shelf of free tools for finding and understanding Bitcoin in Texas — merchant and community maps (BTC Map), the reachable-node census (bitnod.es), ERCOT grid data, and the state's policy bodies. Reference tools only: no exchanges, brokers, or referral links.

## Archive (direct link only)

- [The Wider Ledger — Texas Crypto Archive](https://texasbitcoin.com/texas-crypto-archive): The wider Texas digital-asset story, kept off the main navigation by design — altcoins, developers, and venture capital: Factom's Bitcoin-anchored data layer from Austin (2014), hashgraph/Hedera born in Richardson's Telecom Corridor (2015), Multicoin Capital's early Solana call (2017), 8VC's HQ move to Austin (2020), ATX DAO's civic experiment (2021), the Austin City Council's twin crypto/blockchain resolutions (March 2022), Consensus convening in Austin (2023–2024), the Ethereum Austin and Solana developer scenes (ETH Austin 2022–23, the Solana Hacker House and Helium's Solana migration, April 2023), and where the venture capital went next (Breyer Capital's 2020 Austin move, Multicoin's 56% AUM growth in 2024, the DePIN/AI rotation). 29 cited sources.
